The AI chip supply chain in brief

The fifteen stages that turn sand and software into an AI accelerator: who leads each one, how concentrated it is, and where China and the United States stand.

Download the PDF 4 pagesRead the full chain

Updated 19 October 2026 · Every figure is cited in the chapter each card links to

The chain at a glance

8 of 15 stages are rated Extreme concentration, meaning three or fewer firms could supply each of them today, or one firm holds more than half of it.

StageConcentrationSubstitutabilityWho leads
  1. 01Chip Design, EDA and IPExtremeHardSynopsys US, Cadence US
  2. 02Silicon and WafersHighModerateShin-Etsu Handotai JP, SUMCO JP
  3. 03Chemicals, Gases and PhotoresistHighModerateJSR JP, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo JP
  4. 04LithographyExtremeVery hardASML NL, Nikon JP
  5. 05Photomasks and PelliclesExtremeHardAGC JP, Hoya JP

Concentration counts the firms that credibly supply a stage: Extreme, High, Moderate or Low. Substitutability rates how hard it would be for a well-funded state or firm to build an alternative: Easy, Moderate, Hard or Very hard.

The fifteen stages

In the order a chip is made.

01Stage 1 of 15

Chip Design, EDA and IP

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA sell the software used to design every leading-edge AI accelerator. In 2025 they took over 85 percent of an $18 billion market, licensed blocks included.

Who leads

  • Synopsys US90%+ of the timing-signoff market
  • Cadence US55%+ of the hardware emulator market
  • Siemens EDA US85%+ of physical verification, the final layout check

China

China designs its own AI accelerators, but Huawei's best, the Ascend 950, delivers about half the computing performance of Nvidia's H100 from 2022, on Epoch AI's estimate. CSET found in 2021, from 2019 data, that Chinese design software largely did not support processes at 14 nm and below.

United States

The United States has the two largest design-software vendors and the leading custom-chip design houses.

Read the chapter, with its sources

02Stage 2 of 15

Silicon and Wafers

High concentrationModerate to substitute

Firms based in Japan, Taiwan, Germany and South Korea make most 300 mm wafers used for advanced chips. China makes most polysilicon, almost all of it for solar cells.

Who leads

  • Shin-Etsu Handotai JPIts parent's electronics materials segment, wafers included, had ¥1,015.7bn of sales in the year to March 2026
  • SUMCO JP¥409.7bn of 2025 net sales, but an ¥11.8bn loss
  • GlobalWafers TWNT$60.6bn revenue in 2025

China

China made about 93 percent of the world's polysilicon in 2023. Chinese firms held under 1 percent of the 300 mm wafer market as of 2019.

United States

No major US-headquartered firm makes wafers. GlobalWafers of Taiwan won CHIPS awards of up to $406 million for wafer plants in Texas and Missouri.

Read the chapter, with its sources

03Stage 3 of 15

Chemicals, Gases and Photoresist

High concentrationModerate to substitute

Japanese companies held 78 percent of world photoresist sales in 2023. Supply of chip chemicals, gases and metals has been disrupted three times since 2019.

Who leads

  • JSR JPA vehicle of the state-backed Japan Investment Corporation bought 84.36% of JSR in April 2024
  • Tokyo Ohka Kogyo JPResist maker with ¥139,668m of sales in the first half of fiscal 2026
  • Air Liquide FR€2,465m of electronics revenue in 2025, 9.1% of group sales

China

In March 2026 the Chinese resist maker Hubei Dinglong said China had yet to reach large-scale production of advanced resist for 248 nm, 193 nm or extreme-ultraviolet printing. Since August 2023 China has required licenses to export gallium and germanium.

United States

In photoresist, American companies ranked a distant second to Japanese companies by sales in 2023. In 2021 JSR of Japan agreed to buy Inpria, an Oregon maker of resist for extreme ultraviolet.

Read the chapter, with its sources

04Stage 4 of 15

Lithography

Extreme concentrationVery hard to substitute

ASML, a Dutch firm, is the only maker of extreme ultraviolet scanners, the machines that print the finest layers of a chip. It sold 48 of them in 2025.

Who leads

  • ASML NL100% of EUV (extreme ultraviolet) and above 80% of DUV (deep ultraviolet)
  • Nikon JP22 new chip lithography systems in the year to March 2026
  • Canon JP234 chip lithography systems in 2025, 188 of them i-line and 46 KrF

China

In September 2025 CSIS judged that EUV remained firmly out of reach for China despite massive state investment. SMEE, the older Chinese supplier, has its largest share in i-line scanners, the coarsest kind, and even there holds about 4 percent of the world market.

United States

No American firm makes scanners. But the US government limits who may buy them, through rules on the American-made parts inside each machine and through its entity list of firms that may not be supplied.

Read the chapter, with its sources

05Stage 5 of 15

Photomasks and Pellicles

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Only three firms in the world make the blank plates for the masks used to print the finest layers of leading-edge chips. Japan's AGC and Hoya are two of them.

Who leads

  • AGC JPRanks itself No.2 worldwide in EUV mask blanks on its own fiscal 2026 estimates
  • Hoya JPSays its share of mask blanks is exceptionally high
  • Lasertec JPLaunched the world's first tool that inspects patterned EUV masks at the scanner's own wavelength (2019)

China

SMIC runs two mask shops of its own in Shanghai. No Chinese firm appears in CSET's 2025 market shares for electron-beam mask writers, the machines that draw the pattern onto a mask.

United States

Photronics calls itself one of the world's leading photomask makers, and KLA makes mask inspection tools.

Read the chapter, with its sources

06Stage 6 of 15

Deposition and Etch

High concentrationModerate to substitute

Deposition and etch tools build a chip layer by layer. They are among the chipmaking tools where Chinese toolmakers gained the most share from 2019 to 2024.

Who leads

  • Applied Materials US$28.4B revenue, fiscal 2025; leader in physical and chemical vapor deposition
  • Lam Research US$23.2B revenue, fiscal 2026; leader in conductor etch
  • Tokyo Electron JP23% of dry etch and 38% of tube and low-pressure CVD, 2025

China

Chinese toolmakers held 12.4 percent of dry etch in 2025, according to CSET's analysis of TechInsights data. CSET's earlier analysis had them under 1 percent of atomic layer deposition in 2024.

United States

The US government lists some dry etch, atomic layer deposition and deep-hole deposition tools as controlled exports. Its December 2024 foreign direct product rule reaches some tools built outside the United States.

Read the chapter, with its sources

07Stage 7 of 15

Metrology and Inspection

High concentrationModerate to substitute

KLA, an American firm, held 56.8 percent of the market for tools that measure and inspect wafers in 2025 by CSET's count, about five times its nearest rival.

Who leads

  • KLA US56.8% of process control tools in 2025 by CSET's count, about 5 times Applied Materials
  • Applied Materials US11.2% of process control tools in 2025
  • Lasertec JP6.4% of process control tools in 2025, almost all of it mask inspection

China

Chinese makers are still small in metrology and inspection, but one of them is growing fast. Skyverse, a Shenzhen maker of inspection and metrology tools, reported 2.05 billion yuan of revenue in 2025, about $285 million and up 48.75 percent on 2024.

United States

KLA is the largest maker of metrology and inspection tools in the world. Citing Gartner, KLA puts its 2024 share at 56.5 percent, or 6.5 times its nearest rival.

Read the chapter, with its sources

08Stage 8 of 15

Transistors and the Front End

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Only TSMC, Intel and Samsung make 2 nm-class transistors in volume. TSMC plans its A14 process for 2028, with more than 20 percent higher logic density than N2.

Who leads

  • TSMC TWN2 in volume production since 4Q25, TSMC's first nanosheet node
  • Intel US18A in high-volume manufacturing
  • Samsung Foundry KRFirst into production with gate-all-around nanosheets, starting initial 3 nm output in June 2022

China

SMIC ships a process it calls N+3, measured at 113.4 million transistors per square millimeter. It prints its tightest layers in several passes because it cannot buy an extreme-ultraviolet scanner.

United States

Intel runs the only American-owned line that makes the newest transistors. Its 18A process brought gate-all-around transistors and backside power to market together.

Read the chapter, with its sources

09Stage 9 of 15

Foundries and Fabs

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

TSMC's six largest plants are all in Taiwan. In 2025 they could make more than 13 million wafers a year, out of more than 17 million for the whole company.

Who leads

  • TSMC TW77% of wafer revenue from 7 nm and below, 2Q26
  • Intel Foundry US$5.8bn segment revenue, only $293m of it from outside customers, 2Q26
  • Samsung Foundry KROver $37bn planned in Texas (CHIPS award, Dec 2024)

China

Georgetown University's CSET reported in June 2024 that Huawei's Ascend 910B AI chip is believed to be made on SMIC's 7 nm-class N+2 process. But SemiAnalysis judged in April 2025 that most 910B and 910C chips were made at TSMC.

United States

Intel says it is the only chipmaker that develops and manufactures leading-edge logic chips in the United States. The US government bought a passive 9.9 percent stake in Intel in August 2025, and Intel Foundry lost $2.089 billion in the second quarter of 2026.

Read the chapter, with its sources

10Stage 10 of 15

Memory and HBM

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

SK hynix, Samsung and Micron make nearly all high bandwidth memory (HBM), the stacked memory beside AI chips. SK hynix took 63.2 percent of HBM revenue in 2025.

Who leads

  • SK hynix KR63.2% of HBM revenue in 2025
  • Samsung KR19.3% of HBM revenue in 2025
  • Micron US17.4% of HBM revenue in 2025

China

The Institute for Progress estimated in October 2025 that China would make virtually no HBM that year. Huawei said in September 2025 that its Ascend 950 chips would use two HBM designs of its own, without saying who would manufacture the memory.

United States

Micron is the only American HBM maker. License Exception HBM lets exporters headquartered in the United States or a Country Group A:5 ally ship HBM below 3.3 GB per second per square millimeter without a license.

Read the chapter, with its sources

11Stage 11 of 15

Advanced Packaging

Extreme concentrationModerate to substitute

Epoch AI estimates that in 2025 Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon used around 90 percent of the capacity for CoWoS, TSMC's packaging for AI chips.

Who leads

  • TSMC TWCoWoS packaging used by Nvidia, Google, AMD and Amazon
  • Intel USFoveros 3D packaging in volume at Rio Rancho, New Mexico; EMIB 2.5D bridges
  • ASE Technology TWNT$389.2B assembly, test and materials revenue, 2025

China

Between 2019 and 2024, Chinese firms gained 5 percentage points of share in test tools and 4 points in fabrication tools built for advanced packaging. But they lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States

Intel opened Fab 9 in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, in January 2024 to make its Foveros 3D packages in volume. Amkor is building a $7B packaging and test plant in Peoria, Arizona, and expects production to start in early 2028.

Read the chapter, with its sources

12Stage 12 of 15

Substrates and PCBs

Extreme concentrationHard to substitute

Ajinomoto, a Japanese food company, told investors in June 2026 that it holds over 95 percent of the market for the insulating film inside high-end chip packages.

Who leads

  • Ajinomoto JPTold investors that its build-up film has held over 95% of its market since launch
  • Nitto Boseki JPClaims an overwhelming advantage in low thermal expansion glass
  • Ibiden JPSays it typically takes close to 100% of each new generation of interposer-type substrates at launch

China

TTM, an American circuit board maker, says its circuit board competitors are mostly based in China and Taiwan. Nitto Boseki, a Japanese glass fiber maker, says Chinese and Taiwanese companies are aggressively catching up with it in the special glass sector.

United States

The White House's 2021 supply chain review listed no American firm among the key substrate makers. The Commerce Department has made a final award of up to $75 million to Absolics, a subsidiary of Korea's SKC, for a glass substrate plant in Covington, Georgia.

Read the chapter, with its sources

13Stage 13 of 15

Test and Assembly

High concentrationModerate to substitute

Testing finds bad chips before they go into an expensive package. Japan's Advantest took about 65 percent of 2025 spending on chip testers, by its own estimate.

Who leads

  • Advantest JPAbout 65% of the tester market in 2025, by its own estimate
  • Teradyne USSecond in testers, with $2.52bn of semiconductor test revenue in 2025, service included
  • ASE TWLargest assembly and test contractor; $20.6bn of 2025 revenue, about 59 percent from packaging and test

China

CSET at Georgetown finds that between 2019 and 2024 Chinese toolmakers gained share in test tools and 4 percentage points in fabrication tools built for advanced packaging. But they lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States

American firms such as Teradyne and FormFactor are strong in test machines and probe cards. Amkor is building a $7 billion packaging and test campus in Arizona and has a long-term deal to run packaging and test there for TSMC.

Read the chapter, with its sources

14Stage 14 of 15

Systems and Networking

High concentrationModerate to substitute

AI chips are wired together 72 to a rack and run as one computer. Many firms can assemble the racks, but few can make the lasers for the optical links between them.

Who leads

  • Nvidia USNVLink and NVSwitch for links inside a rack; InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet between racks
  • Broadcom USTomahawk switch chips sold to any buyer, and custom AI accelerators
  • Foxconn TWWorld's largest AI server provider, by its own account; building a factory in Houston

China

Chinese firms such as InnoLight assemble high-speed optical modules in volume, at sites including Suzhou and Thailand. In February 2025 China put indium under new export restrictions and began requiring export permits for indium phosphide substrates, the wafers the lasers are grown on.

United States

American firms make the switch chips, the links that join accelerators inside a rack, and the lasers. Nvidia said in August 2026 that Wistron's new plant in Fort Worth, Texas, was producing its GB300 superchips and that Foxconn was building a factory in Houston.

Read the chapter, with its sources

15Stage 15 of 15

Data Centers and Power

High concentrationModerate to substitute

By mid-2026, Texas had requests to connect about 474 GW of new demand, mostly data centers, but only about 205 GW had the engineering studies to plan for it. The large transformers that connect such sites to the grid commonly took three years to arrive in 2024.

Who leads

  • GE Vernova USGas equipment, transformers and switchgear, including through Prolec GE
  • Hitachi Energy CHPower transformers and switchgear
  • Siemens Energy DEGrid technologies, transformers, turbines

China

China used 25 percent of the world's data center electricity in 2024, second to the United States, by the International Energy Agency's estimate. Data centers made up around 3 percent of the growth in China's electricity demand from 2022 to 2024.

United States

The United States has the demand and the money but cannot shorten the wait for equipment. Constellation expects to restart the Crane nuclear plant for Microsoft in 2027.

Read the chapter, with its sources

Across the chain

Two chapters that are not stages. They look across all fifteen, at what a chip costs and at the contest over who controls them.

16Across the chain

The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

Reports in March 2024 put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins. It says Nvidia's Blackwell margin may therefore be lower than the gap between cost and price suggests.

Read the chapter, with its sources

17Across the chain

Who Controls the Chain

Since 2018 the United States has used export controls to limit China's access to advanced chips and chipmaking tools, and China has been building its own.

Japan and the Netherlands have aligned their own export controls with the American rules on chipmaking equipment. Chinese toolmakers supplied 35 percent of China's own chipmaking equipment market in 2025, up from 10 to 15 percent before 2022. When the United States licensed sales of Nvidia's H200 chip in February 2026, China restricted them.

Read the chapter, with its sources

16 The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

Reports in March 2024 put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins. It says Nvidia's Blackwell margin may therefore be lower than the gap between cost and price suggests.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/component-costs/

17 Who Controls the Chain

Since 2018 the United States has used export controls to limit China's access to advanced chips and chipmaking tools, and China has been building its own.

Japan and the Netherlands have aligned their own export controls with the American rules on chipmaking equipment. Chinese toolmakers supplied 35 percent of China's own chipmaking equipment market in 2025, up from 10 to 15 percent before 2022. When the United States licensed sales of Nvidia's H200 chip in February 2026, China restricted them.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/geopolitics/

13 Test and Assembly

High concentration · Moderate to substitute

Testing finds bad chips before they go into an expensive package. Japan's Advantest took about 65 percent of 2025 spending on chip testers, by its own estimate.

  • Advantest Japan. About 65% of the tester market in 2025, by its own estimate
  • Teradyne United States. Second in testers, with $2.52bn of semiconductor test revenue in 2025, service included

China CSET at Georgetown finds that between 2019 and 2024 Chinese toolmakers gained share in test tools and 4 percentage points in fabrication tools built for advanced packaging. But they lost share in bonding and other conventional assembly and packaging tools.

United States American firms such as Teradyne and FormFactor are strong in test machines and probe cards. Amkor is building a $7 billion packaging and test campus in Arizona and has a long-term deal to run packaging and test there for TSMC.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/test-and-assembly/

14 Systems and Networking

High concentration · Moderate to substitute

AI chips are wired together 72 to a rack and run as one computer. Many firms can assemble the racks, but few can make the lasers for the optical links between them.

  • Nvidia United States. NVLink and NVSwitch for links inside a rack; InfiniBand and Spectrum-X Ethernet between racks
  • Broadcom United States. Tomahawk switch chips sold to any buyer, and custom AI accelerators

China Chinese firms such as InnoLight assemble high-speed optical modules in volume, at sites including Suzhou and Thailand. In February 2025 China put indium under new export restrictions and began requiring export permits for indium phosphide substrates, the wafers the lasers are grown on.

United States American firms make the switch chips, the links that join accelerators inside a rack, and the lasers. Nvidia said in August 2026 that Wistron's new plant in Fort Worth, Texas, was producing its GB300 superchips and that Foxconn was building a factory in Houston.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/systems-and-networking/

15 Data Centers and Power

High concentration · Moderate to substitute

By mid-2026, Texas had requests to connect about 474 GW of new demand, mostly data centers, but only about 205 GW had the engineering studies to plan for it. The large transformers that connect such sites to the grid commonly took three years to arrive in 2024.

  • GE Vernova United States. Gas equipment, transformers and switchgear, including through Prolec GE
  • Hitachi Energy Switzerland. Power transformers and switchgear

China China used 25 percent of the world's data center electricity in 2024, second to the United States, by the International Energy Agency's estimate. Data centers made up around 3 percent of the growth in China's electricity demand from 2022 to 2024.

United States The United States has the demand and the money but cannot shorten the wait for equipment. Constellation expects to restart the Crane nuclear plant for Microsoft in 2027.

Sources: chipsupplychain.org/data-centers-and-power/
